record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: Consider the Birkhoff billiard inside a closed smooth strictly convex hypersurface S in R^d, and let A be the space of all oriented lines intersecting S. For dimensions d ≥ 3, does there exist a billiard table S different from an ellipsoid for which the billiard map leaves invariant a smooth hypersurface Σ in A? If such invariant hypersurfaces exist, what geometric and dynamical properties can they have?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to have an example of the billiard table (different from ellipsoids) S ⊂ R^d having an invariant hypersurface Σ ⊂ A. What are geometric/dynamical properties of those Σ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d\ge 3$) be a closed smooth strictly convex hypersurface, and consider the Birkhoff billiard inside $S$: a point moves along straight lines inside $S$ and reflects off $S$ according to the law of equal angles. Identify the phase space with $\mathcal{A}$, the space of oriented lines in $\mathbb{R}^d$ that intersect $S$, and let $T:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}$ denote the billiard map (sending an incoming oriented line to the outgoing oriented line after one reflection at $S$). When $S$ is an ellipsoid, the billiard map has a smooth foliation by invariant hypersurfaces $\Sigma\subset\mathcal{A}$ corresponding to confocal caustics.

(a) Does there exist a closed smooth strictly convex hypersurface $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d\ge 3$) which is not an ellipsoid, such that the associated billiard map $T$ admits a smooth invariant hypersurface $\Sigma\subset\mathcal{A}$ (i.e., a smooth codimension-one submanifold with $T(\Sigma)=\Sigma$)?

(b) For any such $\Sigma$, describe its possible geometric and dynamical properties (e.g., whether $\Sigma$ must arise from a caustic, the regularity and topology of $\Sigma$, and the qualitative behavior of $T|_\Sigma$).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on higher-dimensional Birkhoff billiards still treats the existence of invariant hypersurfaces for non-ellipsoidal smooth strictly convex tables as an open question. Berger's theorem rules out caustics for non-ellipsoidal tables in dimension ≥ 3, but invariant hypersurfaces not coming from caustics are not excluded, and no example is known. Recent advances (e.g., integrable cone billiards, outer-billiard invariant hypersurfaces for self-polar bodies) concern different settings and do not resolve the Birkhoff case.

status_evidence.title: Gutkin billiard tables in higher dimensions and rigidity
status_evidence.snippet: Only ellipsoids have caustics in higher dimensions; existence of invariant hypersurfaces not from caustics remains open.
status_evidence.claim: For higher-dimensional Birkhoff billiards only ellipsoids have caustics; existence of invariant hypersurfaces not coming from caustics is an open question.

status_evidence.title: Outer billiards of symplectically self-polar convex bodies
status_evidence.snippet: Provides invariant hypersurfaces for outer billiard maps, contrasting with the Birkhoff case where the question remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: New invariant hypersurfaces are known for outer billiards, but the Birkhoff analogue in dimension >=3 beyond ellipsoids remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Integrability of Billiards Inside Cones
status_evidence.snippet: First completely integrable billiard not built from quadrics, but in a non-smooth/non-strictly-convex setting.
status_evidence.claim: Known integrable examples beyond quadrics exist only in degenerate (non-smooth, non-strictly-convex) settings.
